The user has provided very detailed requirements, so I can proceed with creating the plan document. Let me structure it according to the protocol's output format.# Rich Text Editor Toolbar Accessibility Design Plan > **For Claude:** Use a11y-planner protocol. Review with a11y-critic after implementation. > **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA > **Users who need accessibility:** Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver), keyboard-only users, low vision users > **Assistive technologies:** NVDA (Windows), JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS) **Feature:** A toolbar component in a rich text editor containing 24 formatting buttons organized into 4 groups. The toolbar acts as a single tab stop with arrow-key internal navigation via roving tabindex. Some buttons are toggles (Bold, Italic, Underline); others open dialogs (Insert Image, Insert Link). **Risk Level:** High — composite widget with roving tabindex, mixed toggle/action button types, dialog focus restoration, integration with editor focus management. **Component/Page Type:** Toolbar (APG: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/) --- ## Scope & Context ### What is being built A rich text editor toolbar that serves as a single tab stop in the page's tab order. It contains 24 formatting buttons across 4 logical groups (Text Style, Alignment, Lists, Insert). Within the toolbar, arrow keys navigate between buttons using roving tabindex. Some buttons are toggle buttons with `aria-pressed` state; others open modal dialogs and require focus restoration when those dialogs close. ### User needs - Keyboard-only users need to enter the toolbar once (Tab), then use arrows to reach any button without 24 Tab presses - Screen reader users need clear group labels, button names, and pressed states announced - Power users expect Home/End for quick navigation within the toolbar - Users opening dialogs from action buttons need focus returned to the triggering button when the dialog closes ### Compliance target WCAG 2.2 AA (default) ### Assistive technologies supported NVDA (Windows), JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS), keyboard-only users ### Risk factors 1. **Role ambiguity**: Mockup labels it "Format Menu" but there are no submenus — role must be `toolbar`, not `menubar` 2. **Mixed button types**: Toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`) and action buttons (dialog openers) in the same roving tabindex scheme 3. **Group navigation**: Whether arrows step through every button or jump between groups is a design decision requiring explicit specification 4. **Dialog focus restoration**: Action buttons that open dialogs must return focus to themselves when closed, without breaking the toolbar's roving tabindex state ### Constraints - Must support 24 buttons across 4 groups - Some buttons are toggles (Bold, Italic, Underline) with pressed/unpressed state - Others are action buttons (Insert Image, Insert Link) that open dialogs - Design mockup says "Format Menu" but there are no submenus — label ≠ role - Must integrate with existing rich text editor focus management (editor ↔ toolbar ↔ sidebar) --- ## Semantic Structure Plan ### Landmark regions and document structure The toolbar is a child of the main editor region. The overall page structure should be: ```html Skip to main content
``` ### Heading hierarchy No headings are needed within the toolbar itself — it is a widget, not a section of content. The page's main heading (e.g., `

Document editor

`) provides context for screen reader users entering the editor region. ### WCAG citations for semantic structure - **WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships**: Toolbar uses `role="toolbar"`, groups use `role="group"` with `aria-label` to communicate logical grouping programmatically - **WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value**: Each button has a clear accessible name; toolbar and groups have labels ### Structure diagram (HTML stub) ```html
``` --- ## Interaction Pattern Design ### Role decision: `role="toolbar"` vs `role="menubar"` **Decision: Use `role="toolbar"`.** The APG Toolbar pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/) is the correct choice because: 1. **No submenus exist**: The component has 24 flat buttons with no hierarchical menu structure. Menubar's Down-arrow-to-open-submenu behavior does not apply. 2. **Toolbar pattern keyboard model matches requirements**: Left/Right arrows navigate between controls, Tab exits the toolbar — exactly what is needed. 3. **"Format Menu" in mockup is a visual label, not a semantic role**: The design team named it "Format Menu" for UI labeling purposes, but roles are determined by interaction semantics, not visual labels. Using `role="menubar"` would mislead screen reader users into expecting submenu behavior (Down arrow opens submenu) that does not exist. **Why `role="menubar"` is wrong:** - APG Menubar pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/) expects Down/Up arrows to open submenus for top-level items. Since there are no submenus, this behavior would be confusing or non-functional. - Screen readers announce "menu bar" and expect menu item semantics with submenu navigation cues. - The APG Toolbar pattern explicitly states: "A toolbar is a container of controls... Toolbars group related controls so they are easy to find." This matches the 4-group structure perfectly. ### Interactive Elements Table | Widget | APG Pattern | Keyboard Model | ARIA Attributes | WCAG Citation | |--------|-------------|----------------|-----------------|---------------| | Toolbar container | [Toolbar](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/) | Tab enters, Tab exits; Left/Right navigate within | `role="toolbar"`, `aria-label` | 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | Group container | [Toolbar Grouping](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/examples/conditional-presentation/) | No direct keyboard; containers for screen reader orientation | `role="group"`, `aria-label` | 1.3.1 Info and Relationships, 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | Toggle button (Bold/Italic/etc.) | [Toggle Button](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/examples/toggle-button/) | Enter/Space toggles state; Left/Right navigate via roving tabindex | ``) - **Icon-only buttons** (if any): Must use `aria-label` to provide an accessible name since there is no visible text. Example: `` ### Group labeling strategy Each of the 4 groups must have a clear label via `role="group"` + `aria-label`: | Group | Label (aria-label) | Rationale | |-------|-------------------|-----------| | Text Style group | "Text style" | Describes Bold, Italic, Underline, etc. | | Alignment group | "Text alignment" | Describes Align left, center, right, justify | | Lists group | "Lists" | Describes Bulleted list, Numbered list, indent controls | | Insert group | "Insert" | Describes all insertion buttons (link, image, table, etc.) | ### Toolbar labeling strategy The toolbar container must have `aria-label="Formatting toolbar"` — NOT "Format Menu": - **Why not "Format Menu"**: The mockup's visual label is irrelevant to the semantic role. Using a menu-related name would mislead screen reader users into expecting menu behavior (submenus, Down-arrow navigation). - **"Formatting toolbar"** accurately describes both the purpose and the widget type, aligning with the `role="toolbar"` semantics. ### Link text quality for action buttons Action buttons that open dialogs must have descriptive names: | Button | Accessible Name | Rationale | |--------|----------------|-----------| | Insert link button | "Insert link" | Clear about what will happen | | Insert image button | "Insert image" | Clear and specific | | Insert table button | "Insert table" | No ambiguity | ### Language attributes ```html ``` The root `` element must have `lang` attribute. If any button labels contain foreign language text, wrap them in ``. --- ## Testing Strategy ### Automated testing (axe-core) Run axe-core on the toolbar in all states: - **Default state**: All buttons present, roving tabindex correct (`tabindex="0"` on one button, `"−1"` on others) - **After arrow navigation**: Verify `tabindex` values updated correctly - **Toggle pressed state**: Verify `aria-pressed` is set correctly - **Dialog open state**: Verify focus trap and `aria-modal` **What axe-core will NOT catch:** - Focus management correctness (does Tab actually move to the right button?) - Arrow key navigation behavior (Left/Right work, wrapping works) - Home/End functionality - Screen reader announcement quality - Roving tabindex state persistence across tab-out/tab-in cycles ### Static analysis (eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y) Plan as a CI gate for the React component: - Catches missing `aria-label` on icon-only buttons - Catches invalid ARIA attribute usage - Note known false positives: custom `role="toolbar"` wrapper, passthrough props to ` ``` **ARIA Attributes:** - `aria-pressed="true"` when formatting is active (WCAG 4.1.2 Name Role Value) - `aria-pressed="false"` when formatting is inactive - NO `aria-selected` — that's for single-select patterns, not multi-state toggles (APG Toggle Button pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/examples/toggle-button/) **Keyboard Interactions:** - Enter or Space: toggle `aria-pressed` state and apply/remove formatting in editor - Left/Right arrows: handled by parent toolbar's roving tabindex (button should NOT handle these itself) **State Communication:** - When `aria-pressed` changes from `"false"` to `"true"`, screen reader announces "pressed" automatically per WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages - No additional live region needed for simple toggle state changes **Tests:** - Navigate to Bold via arrows → press Space → `aria-pressed` becomes `"true"`; editor applies bold formatting - Press Space again → `aria-pressed` becomes `"false"`; editor removes bold formatting - Multiple toggles can be active simultaneously (Bold + Italic both pressed) — verify this works correctly - Screen reader announces "pressed" / "not pressed" on state change **WCAG Criteria:** - WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard: Enter/Space toggle the button - WCAG 4.1.2 Name Role Value: `aria-pressed` reflects actual state - WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages: state changes are announced to screen readers **a11y-critic review checkpoint:** 🔍 Verify `aria-pressed` (not `aria-selected`), verify toggle behavior works with both Enter and Space, verify multiple toggles can be active simultaneously, verify no redundant visual symbols in the a11y tree. --- ### Task 3: Action buttons that open dialogs with focus restoration 🔍 **Review checkpoint after this task** **Files:** - `components/RichTextEditor/DialogTriggerButton.tsx` (new) - `components/RichTextEditor/ImageInsertDialog.tsx` (new — example dialog) - Integration in existing dialog components to add focus return logic **Structure Stub:** ```tsx ``` **ARIA Attributes:** - No `aria-pressed` — action buttons are not toggles (WCAG 4.1.2) - Plain `
